stories.title: ‘Terror attack from Pak soil will be act of war’: Defence minister Rajnath warns
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh said Thursday India articulated its new policy against terrorism through Op Sindoor, adding that "any terror attack originating from Pakistani soil will be considered an 'act of war' and those contemplating any form of misadventure will be met with deserving response".

Speaking at the News18 Defcon 2026, Rajnath said, "We've made it clear that the nation possesses both 'power of argument' and 'argument of power', and we will communicate through whichever language the other party understands best.
Today, while we work towards establishing global peace, we are simultaneously strengthening our defence capabilities to counter any threat.
Events such as surgical strikes, Balakot strike and Op Sindoor demonstrated that we possess the capability to safeguard our interests."

stories.headline: Teethwal & Sharda Mai
stories.title: Teethwal & Sharda Mai
stories.summary: I visited Tangdhar and Teethwal in 2018. Crossing Sadhna Pass and reliving the memories associated with the Bollywood actress who had interacted with troops in this area after the 1965 war to boost the morale of the soldiers was an experience in itself. Sadhna Pass was formerly called Nastachun, a Kashmiri term associated with the severe cold affecting the nose. The Indian Army has a post here from where one can have a panoramic view of Tangdhar, as well as the triangular-shaped landscape called Madras Hill. I also visited the Zero Point on the bridge connecting India and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (POJK) at Teethwal. Since there is a clear and very close view of the other side, I noticed that there was comparatively little development and infrastructure there. Since much has been written and spoken about the newly constructed Sharda Temple at Teethwal, I decided to revisit the area. The drive from Baramulla to Tangdhar was very smooth, with picturesque landscapes all around. The road infrastructure is of a very high standard. The first welcome change one observes is the infrastructure developed immediately after Sadhna Post. A War Museum, War Memorial, Pahari Culture Museum and a high-standard cafeteria have been built. The view from the Habaksh Viewpoint, named after Brigadier Harbaksh Singh, is breathtaking and mesmerising. Karnah was the largest tehsil of the Muzaffarabad Wazarat before Partition and has a sizable population. The Sikhs live in a village called Tribhoni. The language spoken in the area is Pahari, although some residents also understand Kashmiri. Legend has it that the area was inhabited by Karna, the Mahabharata hero, who named the place Karan-Nah. However, with the passage of time, the name changed to Karnah. Dr Sabar Afaqui, a renowned scholar of POJK, writes in his book Muzaffarabad that Lord Krishna also visited Karnah. The River Kishan Ganga is said to derive its name from Lord Krishna. The area is known for its courageous and resilient people, who have played an important role in defending their land during conflicts with Pakistan, having seen action in 1947–48, 1965 and 1971, as well as during Operation Sindoor. This area boasts two Param Vir Chakras—Lance Naik Karam Singh and Company Havildar Major Piru Singh—and many other gallantry awards. The River Kishan Ganga, also referred to as the Neelum River in POJK, acts as the natural border. Teethwal was an important township and trade centre linking Srinagar with Muzaffarabad and Rawalpindi. The Khatri community and Sikhs, many of whom were goldsmiths, were involved in trade here. After Partition and the subsequent invasion by Kabalis in 1947, part of Karnah came under occupation in POJK. Many families were separated, and the irony is that, at a few places, they can see each other but cannot meet. In 2003, as part of confidence-building measures, people from across the Line of Control (LoC) were able to meet at a place called Chalaina. During the rule of Ashoka, a university named Sharda University is believed to have been established in Karnah, now in POJK, at the confluence of the River Madhumati and the Kishan Ganga. Sharda Peeth Temple is also located there. The temple is revered by Kashmiri Pandits, who recite a daily prayer invoking the deity of learning and seeking blessings: “Namaste Sharade Devi, Kashmira Pura Vasini, Tvam Aham Prarthaye Nityam, Vidya Danam Cha Dehi Me.” Translated, this means: “Salutations to Devi Sharda, who resides in the abode of Kashmir. To you, O Devi, I constantly pray; please bestow upon me the gift of knowledge.” Pilgrims used to undertake an annual yatra to the Sharda Temple through this route, one of the traditional routes. They used to halt at the Dharamshala here. A Gurdwara also coexisted at the same place. During the Kabali Raid, the Gurdwara and Dharamshala were destroyed, and the Khatris and Sikhs migrated. Although the demography of the whole area changed, the land belonging to the Gurdwara remained unoccupied. S. Joginder Singh of village Tribhoni struggled and succeeded in getting this five-marla plot registered as the property of the Sikh community. He subsequently got it fenced with the help of the Army, thus preserving this historic plot. In 2021, Shri Ravinder Pandita of the Save Sharda Committee visited the place and held discussions with S. Joginder Singh and other Sikhs. He proposed constructing a small Sharda Temple and a Gurdwara on this land. Since there are no Sikhs living in this area, the Sikhs of Tribhoni village agreed to and permitted the proposed construction. Presently, a small Gurdwara and temple stand on the land owned by the Sikh community. Subsequently, Ravinder Pandita, through his dedicated and relentless efforts, succeeded in acquiring some additional land adjoining the temple. I attended the customary annual yatra ritual that is held from the temple to the Zero Point on the bridge, and it was a memorable experience. I raised the slogans “Sharda Mata Ki Jai” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” on the bridge, which caught the attention of the Rangers across the river. Across the bridge, the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) runs through this area, and one could distinctly see the infrastructure development that has taken place in recent times. Sringeri Sharda Peetham, the southern cardinal monastery established by Adi Shankaracharya, supported Ravinder Pandita’s efforts for the construction of the temple. At least 20 pilgrims from the South were present and participated in the yatra. The coexistence of the temple and Gurdwara is not only a fine example of interfaith harmony and brotherhood, but also reflects the Sikh community’s respect for other faiths. Jai Sharda Mai. (The author is a former Deputy Assistant Chief of Headquarters Integrated Staff (IT), author and social activist. Feedback: sodhidalbir7777@gmail.com)

stories.headline: J&K horticulture supports 7.5 lakh families: Govt
stories.title: J&K horticulture supports 7.5 lakh families: Govt
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sept 24:Around 35 lakh people from 7.5 lakh families are directly or indirectly linked to J&K’s horticulture sector, which contributes about 10% to the UT’s GDP and generates an estimated ₹12,000 crore annually, the government told the Legislative Assembly. The Agriculture Production Department called horticulture one of the main pillars of J&K’s economy, especially in Kashmir Division. One hectare of orchard area generates approximately 400 man-days of employment annually, the department said, contributing significantly to rural livelihoods. The government confirmed that farmers associated with the horticulture sector have suffered losses in some areas due to natural calamities, including hailstorms, floods and heavy rains. It said the department undertakes assessment of crop losses through field functionaries and extends assistance or relief, wherever admissible, under the provisions of applicable schemes and guidelines. On crop insurance, the reply said the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is presently being implemented in all 20 districts of the UT. The scheme is demand-driven with no cap on the number of farmers to be covered, and all 13.985 lakh Farmer Families of J&K are eligible to avail its benefits, subject to applicable guidelines and eligibility criteria. District-wise details of farmers covered were given in Annexure-A. On pending claims, the government said the major reasons for pendency of genuine claims include Aadhaar non-verification, closure of bank accounts, de-seeding of Aadhaar from the NPCI mapper by banks, and bank accounts being blocked or frozen. It said a special campaign has been launched to resolve such failed payment transactions, under which approximately 60% of the affected farmers have been contacted, with requisite documents being collected from them on a daily basis for verification and further action toward settlement of pending claims. On coverage, the reply said PMFBY covers hailstorm damage to notified crops, including paddy and maize during Kharif and wheat and oilseeds during Rabi. Under the basic cover, the scheme provides area-based insurance against yield losses in standing crops from sowing to harvesting arising from non-preventable risks such as drought, dry spells, floods, inundation, widespread pest and disease attacks, landslides, natural fire due to lightning, storms, hailstorms and cyclones. The scheme thus provides comprehensive protection against major natural perils that may result in crop losses, subject to applicable guidelines and notified crops/areas. On transportation, the department said it has strengthened traffic and logistics management during the peak fruit season through coordinated measures to ensure smooth and timely transportation of horticultural produce. A dedicated Control Room at Qazigund has been established for real-time traffic monitoring, coordination with concerned agencies and dissemination of timely advisories to growers, traders and transporters. Govt said that the Mughal Road is also being utilized as an alternative route, wherever feasible, to reduce congestion on NH-44. Railway parcel/goods/freight services from Anantnag and Budgam to Delhi have been facilitated and promoted for transportation of horticultural produce. These measures, the reply said, have helped diversify the transportation network, reduce dependence on NH-44 and minimize the risk of prolonged stranding of fruit-laden vehicles during the peak harvest season.

stories.headline: J&K Assembly Autumn Session : LPG Heat Reaches Assembly
stories.title: J&K Assembly Autumn Session : LPG Heat Reaches Assembly
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 24: The Jammu & Kashmir government on Thursday announced the approval of a scheme to provide six free LPG cylinder refills every year to families covered under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), triggering a fresh political confrontation in the Legislative Assembly, with the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) terming it “a betrayal”. Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Satish Sharma informed the House about the approval of the scheme aimed at providing cooking fuel support to the poorest households covered under AAY. The announcement, however, immediately led to uproar from the Opposition benches, with BJP members accusing the government of going back on its election commitments and raising slogans against the administration. Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma alleged that the government had promised 12 free LPG cylinders to every household during the election campaign but had now restricted the benefit to six cylinders a year for AAY families. BJP members raised slogans including “Jhooti Sarkaar” and “Yeh dhokha hai” as the issue turned into a heated exchange between the Treasury and Opposition benches. Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather intervened repeatedly and sought to restore order in the House. The LPG scheme itself was first announced in the Jammu and Kashmir Budget 2026-27 presented by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah in February. The Budget proposed six free LPG cylinders annually for all AAY households, describing the measure as direct cost-of-living relief for the “most deprived sections”. The government’s latest announcement comes after questions had been raised earlier in the ongoing Assembly session over the delay in implementing the Budget proposal. In a reply earlier this week, the government had said the proposal was under examination and that the modalities for its implementation were still being worked out. It had indicated that the cost of six domestic LPG refills annually would be reimbursed to eligible AAY families through Aadhaar-enabled Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into their bank accounts. The latest approval therefore marks a shift from the earlier position that the scheme was still under consideration, although details such as the exact commencement date, reimbursement mechanism and other implementation procedures remain important for beneficiaries. According to figures reported in the Assembly earlier this week, around 8.79 lakh AAY families are expected to benefit from the proposed six-refill assistance. The government had not, at that stage, reported any distribution of free cylinders, saying the implementation process was still being worked out. The AAY category covers households identified among the poorest sections under the public distribution system, making the LPG announcement a significant component of the government’s welfare measures. LoP Sharma questioned the government over other commitments, including the promise of 200 units of free electricity and employment for one lakh youth. The Opposition sought answers on the status of these commitments, turning the LPG announcement into a broader confrontation over the Government’s election pledges. The Treasury benches and BJP members traded slogans as the Speaker attempted to bring the proceedings back on track. The disruption added to the already stormy atmosphere surrounding the autumn session, which has witnessed repeated clashes between the Government and Opposition over jobs, power tariffs, regularisation of workers and other public issues. For AAY families, however, the immediate issue is likely to be when the benefit will actually begin and how the reimbursement will reach them. The government’s stated mechanism is DBT-based reimbursement of the cost of six domestic LPG refills annually. This means the implementation will involve verification of eligible beneficiaries, linkage of LPG and bank-account details and establishment of the reimbursement process. The announcement also puts the spotlight on the gap between a Budget announcement and its ground-level implementation. While the six-cylinder benefit was announced in February, the government was still examining its modalities earlier this week. The approval announced in the House now provides a clearer indication that the scheme is moving towards implementation. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday said that six free LPG cooking gas cylinders annually to Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families across Jammu and Kashmir marks the fulfilment of a key assurance made in his second Budget earlier this year. The Chief Minister said the initiative would provide direct relief to the most deserving households and strengthen the government's commitment to public welfare. "This key initiative aims to extend direct relief to the most deserving households, ensuring a dignified life for vulnerable sections and reinforcing the government's commitment to social justice and public welfare," Omar Abdullah said.

stories.headline: JKLA passes resolution on TET exemption for pre-2019 teachers
stories.title: JKLA passes resolution on TET exemption for pre-2019 teachers
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 24: The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the Union government to exempt teachers appointed before January 1, 2019, from appearing in the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). The resolution, moved by Education Minister Sakeena Itoo, received support from both treasury and opposition benches. It seeks amendments to Section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, to provide relief to teachers appointed before the specified date. The move has been welcomed by the teachers’ fraternity, which expressed gratitude to Itoo for taking up their concerns and supporting their demand for exemption from the mandatory test. The resolution urges the Centre to take necessary legal steps and issue a notification through the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) to exempt the teachers from TET. Speaking in the Assembly, Itoo said the resolution would be submitted to the Union Government. She added that the Law Minister would place the matter before the Supreme Court and argue for protecting the dignity of teachers. She said the Education Department had faced considerable pressure to conduct the TET, but the government made efforts to safeguard the interests of teachers. During the discussion, National Conference legislators Nazir Gurezi and Syed Bashir Veeri supported the resolution. Veeri said asking teachers who had already qualified through prescribed recruitment procedures to appear for another test amounted to injustice. He said teachers felt let down when they were asked to take the TET despite having secured their appointments through established selection procedures. Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather observed that the House was unanimous on the issue and called for limiting the discussion. The resolution was subsequently put to a voice vote and passed with support from both sides. stories.headline: Every bill, resolution important: Dy CM
stories.title: Every bill, resolution important: Dy CM
stories.summary: Srinagar: Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Thursday said every bill and resolution brought before the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly carries its own importance, irrespective of whether it is passed or not. Speaking to reporters, Choudhary said the legislative process should ultimately serve the interests of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. “Whether a bill is passed or not, both are important for the government. If a bill has been passed, it is important for us, and if a bill has not been passed, that does not mean the government will not pay attention to it,” he said. He said MLAs from both the treasury and opposition benches consider issues before bringing bills or resolutions in the House, adding that the government takes note of such legislative initiatives and examines them from the perspective of public interest. On the opposition's demand for the resignation of the Election Commission of India (ECI) over allegations raised against the institution, Choudhary said the matter requires attention as the allegations involve an institution in which people have placed their trust. He said the allegations assume significance because they were raised by members of the ECI itself, and called for a clear explanation from the poll body. “The ECI should openly clarify why such allegations have been raised by its own colleagues. The country and its voters are watching,” Choudhary said. He also referred to the constitutional right to vote and said the Election Commission has a responsibility to safeguard the electoral process and people's votes. On the issue of restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir, Choudhary criticised the BJP, alleging that commitments made before Parliament and the Supreme Court had not been fulfilled. He said the J&K government had started implementing commitments made in its manifesto and still had three years remaining in its current term. “We have at least started. It has been two months, we have given six cylinders. We still have three years left. We have given our manifesto for five years,” he said, adding that the government's performance should be assessed when it returns to the people in the 2029 elections. Choudhary also accused the BJP of making repeated claims without fulfilling its commitments, using an analogy of vendors selling household goods in villages to describe what he called misleading promises.
